import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("Stochastic_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 6  # sources
    J = 12  # destinations
    S = 14  # scenarios
    alpha = 0.9  # confidence level
    max_violations = int(math.floor((1 - alpha) * S))

    supplies = [101, 184, 97, 141, 91, 185]
    recourse_caps = [40, 73, 38, 56, 36, 74]
    base_costs = [[21.3, 19.17, 11.27, 8.38, 22.13, 23.02, 8.42, 20.09, 14.65, 22.32, 8.54, 14.7], [19.78, 19.74, 23.85, 24.93, 15.96, 14.54, 13.1, 10.59, 7.13, 6.23, 9.88, 20.09], [8.65, 6.4, 19.45, 15.34, 11.34, 14.57, 5.13, 21.84, 6.05, 14.94, 18.19, 19.51], [23.08, 8.26, 7.72, 11.03, 8.34, 12.64, 8.61, 19.83, 20.4, 19.64, 6.18, 22.75], [13.17, 18.91, 20.28, 6.0, 16.19, 6.96, 22.27, 10.5, 13.38, 5.29, 17.08, 13.38], [6.61, 12.86, 16.2, 15.33, 9.86, 16.97, 5.42, 18.05, 22.6, 10.89, 18.98, 11.73]]
    recourse_costs = [[42.6, 38.34, 22.54, 16.76, 44.26, 46.04, 16.84, 40.18, 29.3, 44.64, 17.08, 29.4], [39.56, 39.48, 47.7, 49.86, 31.92, 29.08, 26.2, 21.18, 14.26, 12.46, 19.76, 40.18], [17.3, 12.8, 38.9, 30.68, 22.68, 29.14, 10.26, 43.68, 12.1, 29.88, 36.38, 39.02], [46.16, 16.52, 15.44, 22.06, 16.68, 25.28, 17.22, 39.66, 40.8, 39.28, 12.36, 45.5], [26.34, 37.82, 40.56, 12.0, 32.38, 13.92, 44.54, 21.0, 26.76, 10.58, 34.16, 26.76], [13.22, 25.72, 32.4, 30.66, 19.72, 33.94, 10.84, 36.1, 45.2, 21.78, 37.96, 23.46]]
    demand_scenarios = [[33, 39, 12, 32, 46, 13, 26, 38, 41, 28, 53, 13], [29, 41, 12, 39, 49, 7, 24, 36, 32, 20, 56, 12], [20, 34, 18, 27, 49, 9, 25, 46, 45, 21, 35, 10], [19, 30, 19, 28, 44, 9, 30, 34, 43, 20, 49, 10], [31, 37, 18, 31, 32, 13, 21, 41, 41, 28, 36, 12], [22, 33, 16, 38, 43, 8, 24, 30, 40, 26, 47, 14], [19, 34, 16, 30, 30, 12, 22, 41, 38, 28, 34, 9], [31, 34, 12, 35, 46, 11, 18, 42, 29, 28, 42, 8], [24, 40, 14, 25, 41, 9, 21, 26, 44, 33, 40, 11], [32, 40, 17, 38, 43, 11, 23, 30, 37, 20, 36, 9], [21, 33, 15, 25, 41, 13, 30, 32, 46, 20, 32, 9], [30, 35, 11, 41, 42, 12, 29, 26, 29, 31, 53, 14], [26, 28, 17, 25, 27, 12, 26, 35, 44, 24, 44, 11], [29, 24, 13, 26, 49, 9, 17, 36, 33, 23, 53, 11]]

    # Big-M: largest demand * 2
    M = max(demand_scenarios[s][j] for s in range(S) for j in range(J)) * 2

    # --- Variables ---
    # Stage 1: base shipments
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Base_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Stage 2: recourse shipments per scenario
    y = {}
    for s in range(S):
        for i in range(I):
            for j in range(J):
                y[(i,j,s)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Recourse_S{i}_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # Violation indicators
    z = {}
    for j in range(J):
        for s in range(S):
            z[(j,s)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Violate_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # --- Objective: minimize base cost + expected recourse cost ---
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(base_costs[i][j] * x[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J))
        + (1.0 / S) * quicksum(recourse_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j,s)]
                               for s in range(S) for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply (base)
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"SupplyBase_S{i}")

    # C2: Supply (recourse per scenario)
    for i in range(I):
        for s in range(S):
            m.addConstr(
                quicksum(y[(i,j,s)] for j in range(J)) <= recourse_caps[i],
                name=f"SupplyRecourse_S{i}_Sc{s}")

    # C3: Demand chance constraint (SAA)
    for j in range(J):
        for s in range(S):
            m.addConstr(
                quicksum(x[(i,j)] + y[(i,j,s)] for i in range(I))
                + M * z[(j,s)] >= demand_scenarios[s][j],
                name=f"DemandChance_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # C4: Violation budget per destination
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(z[(j,s)] for s in range(S)) <= max_violations,
            name=f"ViolationBudget_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

Subject: Two-Phase Shipping Plan Under Demand Uncertainty
To: Operations Leadership Team
From: Supply Chain Director
Date: Today

Challenge
We need a reliable shipping plan that keeps stores in stock despite uncertain customer demand. Being proactive here prevents lost sales, protects customer satisfaction, and reduces last-minute expediting. At the same time, we must control logistics costs and respect warehouse limitations.

Two-Phase Approach
- Phase 1: Commit to a base shipping plan now, before demand is known. This plan positions inventory at stores at the lowest practical cost while staying within each warehouse’s available inventory for base shipments.
- Phase 2: After actual demand is revealed, deploy emergency shipments to cover any shortfalls. These shipments are intentionally more flexible but carry higher unit costs and have their own capacity limits.

Reliability Target
Our service policy requires that each store’s demand be completely covered in most demand scenarios, not necessarily all. We will set the base plan so that, together with emergency options, each store is fully supplied in at least the predefined share of scenarios indicated in the annex. A small number of extreme outcomes may be allowed to miss demand.

Goal
Find the most cost-effective plan that:
- Stays within available warehouse inventory for the base plan and respects separate capacity limits for emergency shipments.
- Ensures each store is fully supplied in most demand scenarios, per our predefined service level.
- Minimizes total expected cost by balancing a prudent base plan with the average emergency shipping required across the range of demand scenarios.

How We Will Proceed
- Build a base plan using known warehouse inventories, store lanes, and baseline shipping costs.
- Stress-test the base plan across all demand scenarios to identify expected shortfalls and where emergency shipments would be needed.
- Size and prioritize emergency channels by lane and warehouse, considering their capacities and higher unit costs.
- Iterate until we reach a plan that achieves the service target in most scenarios while keeping total expected cost low.
- Present the recommended plan with clear trade-offs between higher base positioning versus reliance on emergency shipments.

Key Guardrails
- No warehouse will ship more in the base plan than its available inventory.
- Emergency shipments have separate capacity limits and cost structures.
- Store service must meet the predefined service level across the full set of scenarios.
- We will document any residual risk in the small share of scenarios allowed to miss demand and confirm mitigation options.

Decision Needed
- Confirm acceptance of the service level and the use of emergency shipments for rare, extreme outcomes.
- Approve the implementation of the two-phase plan and the associated monitoring process.
